domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is on-device LLM inference performance, quantization tradeoffs, and serving models via Apple's MLX framework on Apple Silicon. MLX Swift LM is a developer SDK for building on-device AI apps, while Locally AI targets individual consumer productivity on personal devices. Locally AI is a live product on the App Store that was recently acquired by LM Studio, indicating a production-stage system. The content assumes familiarity with iOS development and basic LLM concepts but remains accessible to practitioners. The session is a conference talk with live demonstrations of on-device inference. All supporting evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript from the source transcript.

summary:
Adrien Grondin presents Locally AI, a fully native chatbot app that runs on-device language models on iPhone, iPad, and macOS using Apple's MLX framework, which is optimized for Apple Silicon chips. Gemma 4 by Google is highlighted as a model that runs well on iPhone, particularly the smaller variants. MLX Swift LM is the key GitHub repository for developers building iOS/macOS/iPadOS apps with on-device models; Adrien claims integration takes under 10 minutes with a straightforward API. The broader MLX ecosystem includes MLX VLM (visual models), MLX audio, and MLX video for image/video generation, enabling omni-model use cases like text-to-speech and speech-to-speech.

Models are sourced from the MLX community on Hugging Face, which hosts approximately 4,000-5,000 quantized models, often available within 30 minutes of release. Quantization recommendations range from 4-bit (minimum acceptable quality) to 8-bit (for smaller models); below 4-bit significantly impacts output quality. Liquid models at 300-350 parameters can run in iOS Shortcuts for text processing automations. On latest iPhones, Gemma 4 at 4-bit quantization achieves 40 tokens per second in streaming, offline mode. Older iPhones still achieve around 20 tokens per second, which is useful for many applications.

Locally AI was recently acquired by LM Studio, a local AI model studio supporting downloads from Hugging Face, running models via Llama CPP or MLX, and opening local servers with OpenAI or Anthropic-compatible response types. The app is free on the App Store; the main barrier is model download size (1-3 GB). Tool calling is supported, but structured generation is not yet natively available in MLX Swift LM (third-party packages exist).
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Locally AI Overview
sections.summary: Adrien Grondin introduces himself as developer of Locally AI, a fully native chatbot app that runs on-device models on iPhone, iPad, and macOS using MLX. Gemma 4 by Google is highlighted as a model that runs well on iPhone.

sections.title: MLX Framework and Ecosystem
sections.summary: MLX is Apple's framework optimized for Apple Silicon. MLX Swift LM on GitHub enables iOS/macOS/iPadOS app integration in under 10 minutes. The broader ecosystem includes MLX VLM, MLX audio, and MLX video for multi-modal use cases.

sections.title: Hugging Face MLX Community and Model Selection
sections.summary: Models are sourced from the MLX community on Hugging Face, hosting 4,000-5,000 quantized models often available within 30 minutes of release. Developers grab a model ID and pass it to the MLX Swift LM framework for direct download.

sections.title: Quantization Recommendations and Liquid Models
sections.summary: Recommended quantization is 4-bit to 8-bit; below 4-bit degrades quality. Liquid models at 300-350 parameters can run in iOS Shortcuts for automation and text processing.

sections.title: Performance Demo and App Availability
sections.summary: Live demo shows Gemma 4 at 4-bit quantization running at 40 tokens per second on latest iPhones, streaming and offline. Older iPhones achieve ~20 tokens per second. App is free on App Store; main barrier is 1-3 GB model downloads.

sections.title: LM Studio Acquisition and Q&A
sections.summary: Locally AI was acquired by LM Studio, which supports MLX and Llama CPP with local servers compatible with OpenAI/Anthropic response types. Q&A confirms MLX Swift LM supports tool calling but not yet structured generation natively.
